key_insight: VideoMLA introduces Multi-Head Latent Attention to video diffusion, replacing expensive per-head key/value caches with a shared low-rank latent cache. This can significantly reduce streaming memory and latency for minute-scale autoregressive video generation.
problem_solved: Existing long-rollout video diffusion models still rely on a large sliding-window KV cache, which is a major bottleneck for memory usage and inference speed. Prior work mostly changed which tokens are cached or how positions are encoded, but not the underlying per-head KV layout.
method: Replaces per-head keys and values with a shared low-rank latent representation in the cache.
Adapts Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) to the video diffusion setting for long autoregressive rollouts.
Targets minute-scale generation by reducing the dominant streaming memory and latency costs of KV caching.
impact: For practitioners, this offers a more efficient path to long-form video generation with lower memory footprint and faster inference. It is especially relevant for deploying causal video diffusion systems at longer horizons without scaling hardware costs as aggressively.
